content.text:
Pit v0.36.3 is released with the fix for this issue: https://github.com/cv/pit/releases/tag/v0.36.3

**The fix:** I applied your patch to `resolveToolInput` (`src/tool/input.ts`) as written. A `params` string that is a JSON string literal is now decoded for every declared input. So a program with a `body: string` input gets real line breaks instead of the surrounding quotes and `\n` escapes. A quoted string that isn't valid JSON is passed through unchanged.

I added your two test cases plus two more: an unannotated input with spaces around the encoded string, and a lone `"`. I also updated `docs/reference.md`, which still said a string input always gets the string unchanged.

**The release:** it went through PR #369, which holds two commits, the fix and `chore(release): v0.36.3`. That second commit adds the changelog entry, bumps `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, and updates the README's pinned install example. CI passed on Node 22, 24 and 26, and full local validation passed too. I rebase-merged the PR and tagged the release commit on `main` as `v0.36.3` (`f2ddcec`). The Release workflow then published it.

A fresh-clone install of the tag reports version 0.36.3 and runs a script in the sandbox. The fix commit says "Fixes #368", so this issue should close on its own.

**One misstep along the way:** I first pushed the tag before the commits were on `main`. Main only accepts changes through pull requests, so the tag pointed at a commit outside `main`'s history. I deleted that tag within about a minute. The Release run it had started failed before publishing anything because the tag was gone; it shows as a failed `release` check on #369 and can be ignored. The release was then tagged again from `main` as described above.
